categories.name: BUILD-DRIVER (test target is a build target)
categories.definition: The repo's test entry point is a build driver (autotools/make, cmake+ctest, ninja). Compilation of the whole project is unavoidable and is the FRONT-END process, so compiler/linker work both dominates the fence and is visible as `compile`/`pkg/build`. Fence magnitude is set by the project build, not by how many tests were selected — an instance in this class cannot make the fence small.
categories.static_predictors: repo ∈ {jqlang/jq, redis/redis, valkey-io/valkey, micropython/micropython, fmtlib/fmt, nlohmann/json} (= all C and C++, 42 instances, 42 eligible). Predicted composition: compile+link+make ≥ 60% of fence instructions, test-runner < 30%. NO scope gate needed (build intercept dominates: fmt scope 117 and jq scope 28 both gave the two largest fences in the set). `touches_header` refines rebuild breadth ONLY inside C (4/30 fire); it is 12/12 inside C++ and therefore carries zero within-C++ information.
categories.ground_truth_examples: fmt-3248 (C++, compile 97%, 13128 Ginstr — the class maximum) and jq-2681 (C, compile 60% + pkg/build 32% = 92% build work, 65.8 core-s). Both confirmed at process level: jq argv poll = make 1437 + gcc/libtool 1760 samples. Note fmt is 11/12 of all C++ and is header-only, so 'C++ is compile-dominated' must be stated as 'fmt is'.

categories.name: AOT-UNIFIED (one command compiles the closure, then runs)
categories.definition: One command (cargo test, go test) compiles the crate/package dependency closure and then executes the produced binary. Both a compile term and a run term are materially present; WHICH ONE the banked window-tag composition reports is decided by the front-end process name, not by the physics, so this class predicts a MIXTURE and refuses to predict the winner. Fence magnitude = repo-fixed build closure + selected tests; a small module (gin) can produce an unmeasurable fence even though it 'compiles'.
categories.static_predictors: repo ∈ {tokio-rs/tokio, sharkdp/bat, astral-sh/ruff, tokio-rs/axum, nushell/nushell, uutils/coreutils, burntsushi/ripgrep, caddyserver/caddy, gin-gonic/gin, prometheus/prometheus, gohugoio/hugo, hashicorp/terraform} (= all Rust and Go, 85 instances, 47 eligible). Predicted composition: compile ≥ 20% AND runner ≥ 20% (mixed, HHI < 0.65). Scope gate scope ≥ 10 REQUIRED — this class contains the only build-language rejection.
categories.ground_truth_examples: prometheus-9248 (Go, reported compile 62% / tests(go) 28%, 383.3 core-s) and tokio-6551 (Rust, reported tests(rust) 87% / compile 10%, 192.3 core-s). gin-3741 (Go) belongs here and is correctly pre-rejected by the scope gate (scope 2). The mixture claim is the defensible one: tokio's own argv log is compile 1698 vs tests(rust) 775 samples (2.2x compile) while its window composition says 8.7x test — the two disagree in OPPOSITE directions.

categories.name: JVM-UNIFIED (bytecode compile cheap, VM boot + surefire dominate)
categories.definition: maven/gradle compiles a handful of .java files (cheap) and then pays a large fixed cost: JVM start, dependency-classpath resolution from a warm ~/.m2, surefire fork, JIT warmup. The runner tag wins overwhelmingly and compile is a single-digit share. Critically, fence magnitude is nearly INDEPENDENT of test count — this is the class where the static scope feature has no predictive value at all.
categories.static_predictors: repo ∈ {projectlombok/lombok, apache/lucene, google/gson, apache/druid, javaparser/javaparser, reactivex/rxjava} (= all Java, 43 instances, 42 eligible). Predicted composition: tests(java) ≥ 75%, compile ≤ 15%. Scope gate is only scope ≥ 2 (deliberately near-vacuous) BECAUSE the intercept dominates. Do NOT use scope to pick a 'large' Java task.
categories.ground_truth_examples: gson-2061 (tests(java) 88% / compile 7% / java-other 3%, 270.8 core-s — the second-largest fence in the whole reference set) from n_p2p=4, n_f2p=2, scope 6, ps_chars 169 (the corpus 1st percentile). gson is the single most important calibration row in the study: it is the counter-example that kills every static magnitude threshold, since php-cs-fixer has 40x its test scope and 2.6x LESS measured CPU.

categories.name: INTERPRETED-SUITE (no compile; runner + app-under-test)
categories.definition: No compilation anywhere in the test path. Fence CPU is the test runner process plus, frequently, the repo's OWN installed binary being exercised as the subject under test. Fixed cost is near zero (the bundle/vendor tree is prebuilt in the image), so fence magnitude scales roughly linearly with how many tests are selected — this is the ONLY class where the static scope feature works, and consequently the only class that produces magnitude rejections.
categories.static_predictors: repo ∈ {laravel/framework, briannesbitt/carbon, php-cs-fixer/php-cs-fixer, phpoffice/phpspreadsheet, rubocop/rubocop, fluent/fluentd, fastlane/fastlane, jekyll/jekyll, faker-ruby/faker, jordansissel/fpm} (= all PHP and Ruby, 87 instances, 41 eligible). Predicted composition: runner + app-under-test ≥ 90%, compile = 0%. Scope gate scope ≥ 20 REQUIRED (within-PHP measured slope ≈ 0.43 core-s per test, intercept ≈ 5 core-s).
categories.ground_truth_examples: php-cs-fixer-7523 (tests(php) 97%, 105.3 core-s, scope 237) and rubocop-13668 (59.1 core-s, scope 45). rubocop's banked '53% pkg/build (bundler)' is NOT dependency resolution: all 652 of those argv samples across 11 runs are `/usr/local/bundle/bin/rubocop --only Style/SoleNestedConditional -a /tmp/reprodir/t.rb` — the app under test, matched by the tagger regex `\bbundler?\b` hitting the `/bundle/` path component. There is no `bundle install` or `gem` anywhere in the log. Both PHP rejections (carbon-2813, laravel-51890) are also class I and both are caught pre-flight.

categories.name: NODE TRANSPILE+SUITE
categories.definition: A JS/TS test command runs a transpiler or bundler (esbuild, babel, swc, tsc, vite) as a child or in-process, then a JS runner (jest, vitest, mocha). The runner tag absorbs almost everything; a real transpile sub-term exists but is currently mis-tagged. Fixed cost is small-to-moderate, so like class I the magnitude tracks selected tests.
categories.static_predictors: repo ∈ {preactjs/preact, babel/babel, axios/axios, mrdoob/three.js, facebook/docusaurus, vuejs/core, immutable-js/immutable-js} (= all JavaScript and TypeScript, 43 instances, 22 eligible). Predicted composition: tests(js) 70–99%, plus a transpile sub-term of 5–35%. Scope gate scope ≥ 20 REQUIRED.
categories.ground_truth_examples: vue-11915 (TypeScript, reported tests(js) 99% / shell 1%, 214.5 core-s) and babel-15445 (JavaScript, tests(js) 77% / shell 12% / git 8%). vue's banked 'pkg/build' bar is the transpile sub-term hiding in plain sight: 523 of its 532 pkg/build samples are `/testbed/node_modules/.pnpm/@esbuild+linux-x64@0.21.5/.../esbuild`, i.e. a COMPILER routed to pkg/build by the regex `\bpnpm\b` matching a path component.

categories.name: PYTHON-PYTEST (out-of-corpus; retained only to place the three Python reference rows)
categories.definition: pytest-driven suite; CPU in the interpreter plus, in numeric repos, compiled SIMD/BLAS kernels called from Python. Behaves like class I (no build step, magnitude tracks selected tests) with an extra native-kernel term. Listed for completeness of the ground-truth reconciliation; it is NOT a sampling target here.
categories.static_predictors: NOT PRESENT in SWE-bench Multilingual — 0 of 300 candidates (the three reference rows come from the earlier SWE-bench Verified campaigns in local_agents/superseded_40min). No predictor is needed or offered; if a Python repo ever enters the frame, treat it as class I plus a native-kernel flag.
categories.ground_truth_examples: astropy-14096 (pytest 52% / python-other 18% / pkg/build 17% / compile 10% — the most mixed composition measured, HHI 0.34), sympy-14248 (pytest 69% / python-other 21% / shell 7%), scikit-learn-25232 (tests(pytest) 96%, CPU in NumPy/BLAS SIMD kernels). Already banked; no further Y episodes are proposed.

decision_procedure:
DETERMINISTIC, ORDERED. Input = one inventory CSV row. Output = (mechanism, tier, flags, eligibility). Two people with the same row get the same answer.

STEP 0 — MECHANISM (total function of the `repo` column; the 41-repo table in static_predictors above covers all 300 instances, verified: 42 B + 85 A + 43 J + 87 I + 43 N = 300).
  mech = LOOKUP[repo]. If `repo` is not in the table -> STOP, do not classify, extend the table first. Never fall through to a language default.
  Rationale for keying on repo rather than language: within PHP, laravel (6.4 core-s) vs php-cs-fixer (105.3) differ 16x; within Go, gin (137 Ginstr) vs prometheus (383 core-s) differ ~750x. Repo is a CSV column, so this stays fully static.

STEP 1 — HARD EXCLUSIONS (evaluate in this order; FIRST hit wins and the instance is INELIGIBLE; do not continue).
  1a. ps_chars < 150                              -> X-DEGEN   (2/300 instances)
  1b. mech == I and scope < 20                    -> X-SMALL   where scope := n_f2p + n_p2p
  1c. mech == N and scope < 20                    -> X-SMALL
  1d. mech == A and scope < 10                    -> X-SMALL
  1e. mech == J and scope < 2                     -> X-SMALL   (deliberately near-vacuous; see 'J' above)
  1f. mech == B                                   -> no scope test at all
  1g. repo already sampled in this campaign AND this instance is not part of a pre-declared within-repo contrast pair -> X-DUP
  Result on the corpus: 194/300 eligible (B 42, A 47, J 42, I 41, N 22), 2 X-DEGEN, 104 X-SMALL.

STEP 2 — WARN FLAGS (non-exclusive; record all that fire; they never block, they change how the result may be phrased).
  2a. 150 <= ps_chars < 600 -> W-READ. MUST read the problem statement and confirm it names a concrete symbol, API, file or failing test. If it is a bare one-line wish, reclassify as X-DEGEN by hand. (38/300 fire; this is where fmt 380, jq 322, prometheus 462, php-cs-fixer 504, rubocop 528 and gson 169 all live, so this band cannot be auto-excluded.)
  2b. scope < median(scope) over the eligible instances of the same repo -> W-LOWLEV.
  2c. max(scope)/max(min(scope),1) over the repo < 3 -> W-NOLEV: the instance cannot move the fence in this repo; usable only as a negative control (jq 1x, javaparser 1x, immutable-js 1x, nlohmann/json 1x).
  2d. this repo's share of its language >= 0.50 -> W-CONFOUND: report the result at REPO level, never with the language as subject (fires for fmt = 11/12 of C++, preact = 17/31 of JavaScript).
  2e. patch_files >= 3 or patch_hunks >= 8 or patch_add >= 80 -> W-BIGDIFF. Reported covariate on the HARNESS fence only. It is NOT a CPU predictor (jq-2681, the largest patch in the reference set at patch_add 1561 / 71 hunks / 6 files, measured 0% editor CPU).

STEP 3 — TIER (within-repo, because absolute scope is not comparable across repos).
  If W-NOLEV: tier = F (flat). Else tier = tercile of this instance's scope rank among the ELIGIBLE instances of the same repo: bottom third S, middle M, top third L.
  Tie-break for equal scope, applied in order: larger test_hunks, then larger test_add, then lexicographically smaller instance_id.

STEP 4 — LABEL = "<mech>.<tier>", e.g. A.L, I.M, B.F. The sampling frame is 5 mechanisms x 3 tiers = 15 cells (not 45). Every published cell carries n_sampled/n_candidates, n_repos, repo share, and the sampled instance's within-repo scope percentile.

STEP 5 — POST-EPISODE STOP GATE (the only measured step; runs AFTER the paid live episode and BEFORE committing the ~50 min / 11-pass replay).
  Compute the tool-fence total from the live episode's cgroup cpu.stat, EXCLUDING the container-bootstrap interval (drop the apt/dpkg/http lineage — verified contamination: 38 of 261 argv samples in the gin fence, 15%, are `apt-get install -y python3`, `/usr/lib/apt/methods/http`, `dpkg --configure libpython3.10-minimal`).
  Proceed to replay only if ALL hold: corrected fence >= 20 core-s AND >= 1000 Ginstr AND the action-uniqueness gate (E7) passes. Otherwise PARK the episode. This gate is free — the episode is already paid for — and it is the only thing standing between a bad static guess and 50 wasted minutes of exclusive-core time.

SELECTION RULE once labels exist: the 12 banked episodes already cover all 5 sampleable mechanisms and 9 of the 15 cells. Do not spend episodes filling cells. Spend the remaining budget on (i) within-repo S-vs-L pairs in high-leverage repos (prometheus 77x, tokio 42x, lombok 164x, redis 61x, babel 44x, preact 38x, rubocop 18x) which is the only design that can support the 'instance dominates language' claim with repo/language/toolchain held fixed; (ii) one W-NOLEV control (jq, 1x spread) predicting the instance effect vanishes; (iii) 1–2 repeats of one instance to give the spread that the locked 'document spread' convention requires and that every n=1 cell currently lacks.
ambiguity_rule:
The primary axis cannot tie. Mechanism is a total function of `repo` (STEP 0), and each of the 41 repos maps to exactly one mechanism, so no instance can satisfy two mechanisms — this is the whole reason the frame is keyed on repo rather than on overlapping instance predicates. The draft's five predicates were not a partition (measured on the 300 rows: 46% satisfied exactly one, 46% two, 0.3% three, 8% none), and 'one task per cell' was undefined until a priority order was invented. That failure mode is removed by construction, not by a tie-break.

The ties that remain, and their resolution:
1. MULTIPLE WARN FLAGS: they are non-exclusive, all are recorded, none blocks. Precedence matters only for phrasing: W-CONFOUND outranks everything — if it fires, the finding is stated at repo level with the repo named in every figure, table and caption ('fmt (C++, header-only)', never 'C++'), regardless of what else fired.
2. HARD EXCLUSION vs SELECTION SLOT: exclusion always wins. Never relax a threshold to fill an empty cell — that is fitting the frame to the sample. An empty cell is published as empty with a reason code: `—` if structurally impossible, `0 of N` if empirically absent.
3. EQUAL SCOPE WITHIN A REPO (common: jq's 9 instances are all scope 28–29): tier = F if the repo's spread < 3x; otherwise break by test_hunks, then test_add, then lexicographic instance_id.
4. STEP 2a MANUAL OVERRIDE: if a human reader downgrades a W-READ instance to X-DEGEN, the decision and the reason string are recorded in the plot_spec alongside the instance so the exclusion is auditable and not re-litigated.
5. ACTION-MIX vs CPU-MIX AMBIGUITY (the babel case): resolved by definition, not by tie-break. This taxonomy classifies TOOL-FENCE CPU only. Action mix is a reported covariate on a different fence (the harness fence) and never a category. Every task is search/edit-dominated by action count, so that axis is near-constant and carries almost no CPU information: in fmt, compile is 12% of actions and 97% of fence CPU (~237x cost ratio per action); in babel, search is 72% of actions and tests are 77% of CPU. babel is therefore reported as 'class N, test-runner CPU, search-heavy actions' — both numbers, no forced choice.
risk_rule:
Three-layer gate. Layer 1 is free and static; layer 2 is free and unpaid; layer 3 is measured and is the load-bearing one. Validated against all 12 reference rows: it passes all 9 accepts and pre-rejects all 3 rejects, with no static false positives.

LAYER 1 — STATIC PRE-FLIGHT (CSV only; costs nothing).
  R1 DEGENERACY: ps_chars < 150 -> reject. Catches carbon-2813 (124 chars, 12 identical actions, 6.6 core-s). The cut is at 150 and NOT at 600: the corpus p1 is 169 and that is gson-2061, an accepted 270.8 core-s episode. A ps_chars >= 600 filter would have excluded 6 of the 9 accepted references (fmt 380, jq 322, prometheus 462, gson 169, php-cs-fixer 504, rubocop 528) while KEEPING the reject laravel-51890 (741) — precision and recall both bad. 150 loses 2 instances of 300 and is therefore free.
  R2 ZERO-INTERCEPT MECHANISMS: mech ∈ {I, N} require scope >= 20. These are the classes with no compile intercept, so magnitude really does track test count (within-PHP measured slope ≈ 0.43 core-s/test on intercept ≈ 5: scope 3 -> 6.6, 8 -> 6.4, 237 -> 105.3). Catches laravel-51890 (scope 9) and carbon-2813 (scope 4). Passes php-cs-fixer 237, rubocop 45, vue 45, babel 56 — clean separation on all six I/N reference rows.
  R3 SMALL BUILD CLOSURE: mech == A requires scope >= 10. Catches gin-3741 (scope 2, 137 Ginstr). Passes prometheus (12) and tokio (22).
  R4 EXEMPTIONS, STATED AS SUCH: mech == B has NO scope gate and mech == J has an effectively vacuous one, because in those classes the intercept (whole-project build; JVM+maven boot) dominates and a scope threshold would reject good tasks. This asymmetry is the rule's most important feature: any UNIFORM static scope cutoff that rejects gin (2) or laravel (9) also rejects gson (6), the second-largest fence measured. Do not impose one.
  Do NOT use as risk predictors: n_f2p+n_p2p compared ACROSS mechanisms (Spearman +0.32 vs measured core-s, n=10, not significant; php-cs-fixer 237 tests -> 105 core-s vs gson 6 tests -> 271 core-s inverts it), patch_add (Spearman -0.08), touches_build (fires on 3/300 and is 0 on rubocop), touches_core (defined in the extractor as `int(lang in COMPILED)` — a pure language dummy, Spearman +0.08).

LAYER 2 — FREE REPO PROBE (no API spend, no exclusive cores, runs on the housekeeping partition; ~2–10 min per repo, under 2 h for a 15-repo shortlist).
  R5 In the task's own prebuilt SWE-bench docker image, on the UNPATCHED tree, run the repo's install + test command under the 10 Hz cgroup cpu.stat poller only — no model calls, no perf, no replay. This yields a measured fence_floor(repo) = the intercept the static features cannot see. Re-run once with the instance's test_patch applied for fence_hat(instance). Then REPLACE the guessed thresholds in R2/R3 with measured ones, and record per repo whether the test entry point re-resolves dependencies on every invocation (the only honest way to decide whether a dependency-resolution term exists — see known_limits on the deleted D category).
  This probe also pays for itself arithmetically: at the observed 20% rejection rate, each avoided reject saves ~1 h of exclusive-core time that cannot be parallelised (nohz_full + ISO-PROOF silence gate require sole ownership of cores 2–11,14–23).

LAYER 3 — POST-EPISODE STOP GATE (measured; the only layer that cannot be fooled). Identical to STEP 5 of the decision procedure: after the paid live episode and before the 11-pass replay, require bootstrap-corrected tool fence >= 20 core-s AND >= 1000 Ginstr AND action-uniqueness (E7). Bootstrap correction is mandatory, not cosmetic: 15% of gin's fence argv samples are apt/dpkg image bootstrap, so on a 137 Ginstr fence a material share of what was measured is swerex setup rather than agent tool work. gin also has only 1 replay run banked (not 11), so its rejection was in practice this gate firing — codify it instead of relying on noticing.

FLOOR CALIBRATION: 20 core-s comes from the three rejects (6.4, 6.6, and a 137 Ginstr fence, all under 7 core-s) versus the smallest accept (rubocop, 59.1 core-s). The gap 7 -> 59 is wide and unpopulated, so the exact number inside it is not critical; re-derive it once layer-2 probe data exists.
known_limits:
BLUNT LIST. Read this before quoting any cell.

1. THE MECHANISM AXIS IS NEARLY COLLINEAR WITH LANGUAGE. B = all C/C++, A = all Rust/Go, J = all Java, I = all PHP/Ruby, N = all JS/TS. So the mentor's <language x type> grid is NESTED, not crossed: the language determines the mechanism column. Filling a 9x5 grid is therefore not possible in principle, and the 5 mechanism cells are ALREADY 5/5 covered by the 12 banked episodes. The only genuinely within-language axis this spec offers is the within-repo scope tier, and it has real leverage in only some repos (spread 77x prometheus, 164x lombok, down to 1x jq). Anyone expecting 45 informative cells should be told this up front.

2. THREE DRAFT CATEGORIES ARE DELETED, WITH REASONS.
   - E (edit-dominated): deleted. No editor tag dominates CPU in ANY of the 12 measured compositions. jq-2681 has the largest gold patch in the set (1561 added lines, 71 hunks, 6 files) and 0% editor CPU; fmt-3248 has the smallest (3 lines, 1 file) and the highest editor ACTION share (34%). Spearman(core-s, patch_add) = -0.08. Retained only as the W-BIGDIFF covariate on the harness fence.
   - S (search-dominated): deleted as a CPU category. Its predicate fires on 125–152 of 300 depending on thresholds — a stratum containing half the corpus is the background, not a stratum. Its components are near-constant or structurally broken: ps_has_traceback fires 17/300 and is 0.00 by construction for C++, JS, PHP, Ruby and TypeScript (the regex only has `Traceback|panic:|at Foo(x:1)|#N 0x`); ps_has_repro fires 265/300 because the pattern matches any code fence. The six reference tasks satisfying S span the entire outcome space (compile 97%, tests 99%, tests 97%, tests 77%, unmeasurable, IPC-unstable). Search difficulty is real but it lives on the harness fence and in API cost, not in tool-fence CPU.
   - D (dependency-resolution): deleted as an instance category, and the evidence that motivated it does not exist. I re-read the banked logs: all 652 of rubocop's 'pkg/build (bundler)' argv samples across 11 runs are `/usr/local/bundle/bin/rubocop --only Style/... -a /tmp/reprodir/t.rb` — the application under test, matched because the tagger regex `\bbundler?\b` hits the `/bundle/` component of the install prefix. There is no `bundle install` and no `gem` anywhere in that log. Separately, its static predictor touches_build fires on exactly 3/300 (axios-5316, carbon-2813, axum-682), its only PHP member is the rejected degenerate task, and rubocop itself has touches_build = 0: recall 0/1, precision 0/1. Whether a real dependency-resolution term exists anywhere is now an OPEN question to be answered by the layer-2 repo probe, as a repo attribute, not asserted from a mislabelled bar.

3. TWO OF THE TWELVE REFERENCE COMPOSITIONS ARE PARTLY TAGGER ARTEFACTS, SO TWO CATEGORY PREDICTIONS CANNOT CURRENTLY BE FALSIFIED.
   - vue-11915's 'tests(js) 99% / pkg/build' hides a compiler: 523 of 532 pkg/build samples are `.../@esbuild/linux-x64/bin/esbuild`, routed to pkg/build by `\bpnpm\b` matching a PATH component. Class N's transpile sub-term is asserted from this corrected reading, not from the published bar.
   - prometheus-9248's 'compile 62%': its compile bucket is 5234 argv samples of which only 54% are real `pkg/tool/linux_amd64/compile`, while 32% are the COMPILED TEST BINARY `/tmp/go-build*/b001/rules.test` (caught by the `/tmp/go-build` path anchor) and 8% are `go vet`. Corrected, prometheus is much closer to a 50/50 compile-vs-test mixture. That is a NEW defect, not one either reviewer named.
   - tokio-6551: window composition says tests(rust) 87% / compile 10% (8.7x test); its own argv log says compile 1698 vs tests(rust) 775 samples (2.2x compile). The ordering INVERTS. Cause: TAG_PRIORITY ranks all tests(X) above compile and tag_for() assigns one winner per window, so a persistent `cargo test` front-end absorbs its own rustc children, while a `make`/`cargo build` front-end lets compile show. Caveat in the other direction: argv poll counts are not instruction-weighted, so the magnitudes are not directly comparable — only the inversion is. CONSEQUENCE: class A deliberately predicts a MIXTURE and refuses to name the winner, and no B-vs-A boundary should be drawn from the current window compositions until the tagger is fixed (fix argv[0] basename matching, add an app-under-test tag for `*/bin`, `vendor/bin`, `node_modules/.bin`, stop treating `*.test` binaries and `go vet` as compile, and record the full tag MULTISET per window instead of a single winner).

4. THE PREDICTED-COMPOSITION SHARES ARE PRIORS, NOT MEASUREMENTS. Static metadata contains no information about the repo's build intercept. There is no CSV feature for compilation-unit granularity, dependency-closure size, reverse-dependency fan-in of the patched files, JVM/bundler warmup cost, or test selectivity of the harness's command. touches_header is the only feature in that spirit and it is constant inside C++ (12/12, both repos header-only) and repo-confounded inside C (4/30, concentrated in jq/micropython/redis). Every magnitude number in this spec therefore rests on the layer-2 probe or on the layer-3 post-episode gate, never on the CSV.

5. WHAT THE STATIC RULES WOULD GET WRONG. On the 12 reference rows the accept/reject decision is 12/12 correct, but that is 12 points fitted with 4 thresholds — treat it as consistency, not validation. Known soft spots: (a) gson-2061 passes only because class J is exempted from a scope gate, which is a mechanism-level prior, so a Java task with a genuinely trivial suite would slip through; (b) gin-gonic still has 4 instances at scope 10–17 that R3 admits even though the whole gin module is small — flag every gin candidate W-LOWLEV and expect the layer-3 gate to do the real work; (c) the tier assignment for jq is degenerate (all 9 instances at scope 28–29) so jq is labelled B.F and is useful only as the negative control; (d) 104 of 300 instances are excluded as X-SMALL on thresholds derived from 10 measured points — some of those are certainly measurable, and the spec accepts that loss deliberately because the budget is ~14 episodes against 300 candidates, i.e. budget-limited, not sample-limited.

6. CONFOUNDS THAT CANNOT BE FIXED IN THIS CORPUS. C++ has 2 repos (fmt 11 instances, nlohmann/json 1) and BOTH are header-only template libraries, so every test translation unit re-instantiates the library — the pathological end of the C++ build spectrum, not its centre. C++ cannot be de-confounded at any budget here: keep fmt as an explicitly labelled build-extreme case study, phrase it as an existence claim ('at least one C++ task is compile-dominated at 97%'), and exclude C++ from any cross-language comparison figure. Same treatment for JavaScript while preact (17/31) is the only source in a cell. A language-level claim requires >= 2 sampled repos in that language; that is affordable for 8 languages at 1 extra episode each and impossible for C++.

7. EVERY BANKED CELL IS n = 1. No spread can be reported anywhere, which collides directly with the locked convention 'never pool runs — use the median run per cell and document spread'. Also, the headline claim 'the INSTANCE dominates fence size far more than the LANGUAGE' is currently evidenced by fmt (13128 Ginstr) vs gin (137 Ginstr), a pair that differs in language, repo, toolchain, test selectivity AND instance simultaneously — it cannot separate the factors it names. Only the within-repo S-vs-L pairs in STEP 5's selection rule can support that sentence as worded.

8. SCOPE FOR THIS SPEC. It classifies TOOL-FENCE CPU. It says nothing about the harness fence, the litellm proxy (which runs on the housekeeping cores and is excluded from measured-partition capacity claims), or API cost. Kernel threads belong to no cgroup, so all fence totals remain lower bounds bounded by the partition witness and gate E11.
